title: Los Villatoros Harvesting (Mexican H-2A farmworkers)
summary: Los Villatoros Harvesting (LVH), a farm labor contracting company, operated as a criminal enterprise between about 2015 and 2017. It fraudulently recruited Mexican nationals on short-term H-2A agricultural visas, charged exorbitant recruitment fees and lied about pay, hours, working conditions and expense reimbursement. In the US, workers were compelled to do long hours of farm labour six to seven days a week in Florida, Kentucky, Indiana, Georgia and North Carolina, for far less than they were owed. Coercion included imposed debts, confiscated passports, crowded and unsanitary housing, isolation, verbal abuse and threats of arrest, deportation and harm to family in Mexico. In June 2026 Alexander Villatoro Moreno was sentenced to 70 months in prison after pleading guilty to RICO conspiracy; company owner Bladimir Moreno had been sentenced to 118 months in 2022, and co-defendants received 41 months, 37 months and 8 months' home detention.
